details.description: Peach-gold sky transitions into lower-value lavender haze behind the far buttes; soft cloud bands remain atmospheric rather than solid scenery.
Distant vertical buttes use stacked horizontal strata shelves and softened eroded corners with decreasing contrast through depth.
details.affects: far canyon silhouette and atmospheric depth

details.description: The central station stacks a broad gabled base, narrower upper rooms and a steep bell-tower roof into one dominant stepped silhouette.
Repeated narrow arched windows emit restrained amber light from recessed dark openings across the station tiers.
details.affects: inhabited station read and warm/cool separation

details.description: Dark timber posts, cross braces, plank seams and lighter worn edges articulate each gabled volume.
A small star flag, pole finial and visible bell/cupola hardware terminate the station tower.
A dense radial set of tapered metal blades attaches to one hub above the timber trestle and ranch roof.
The cylindrical tank sits on four tall timber legs with cross-braced bays, a conical metal roof and projecting pipework.
Two continuous steel rails form a dark elliptical band with a narrow bright upper highlight and rusty side response.
Closely spaced timber sleepers and small spikes repeat beneath the rails with even path spacing and slight value variation.
Multiple dark wheels with brass rims are linked by a horizontal connecting rod below the blue-black boiler and cab.
White steam exits the chimney while soot-darkening concentrates around the upper stack and boiler seams.
A deep black rail opening cuts through an orange rock mound with a blocky weathered arch and small sign plate above.
details.affects: rail continuity and right-side negative space

details.description: The compact two-storey sheriff office uses a deep porch, square roof lantern, projecting sign silhouette and side fence.
The tall supporting cliff is broken into vertical fins by deep ravines, branching tributaries, stepped shelves and irregular chipped rim blocks around all 360 degrees.
details.affects: pillar depth, canyon network and geological read

details.description: Broken sandstone edges are brighter ochre while recessed cracks and undersides shift to dark terracotta/brown.
Saguaro cacti vary in height, arm count and sage/olive value; longitudinal ribs catch thin highlights.
Short timber fences, crates, barrels, sheds and posts create irregular clusters between buildings and cliff edges without filling every gap.

definitionOfDone: At the approved 390×844 overview the world immediately reads as Cactus Canyon: a broad inhabited summit on a substantial full-width red-rock pillar, one monumental ravine plus smaller 360-degree cuts, a rock-cut public railway, central frontier tower, four distinct satellites, locomotive, cacti and layered sunset buttes.
The real 36-tile route remains complete and readable; railway, buildings, cacti and effects never replace or obscure gameplay geometry.
Left and right orbit views prove non-planar terrain, attached structures, continuous rails and coherent inferred rear construction.
All repeated systems are instanced or merged where practical, High remains within approximately 175 draw calls and 180k triangles, and reduced motion freezes decoration safely.

featureGroups.name: Pillar-supported mesa and rock-cut railway silhouette
qualityCriteria: The broad summit is supported by a substantial fractured mountain pillar whose lower width remains close to the summit width, never a floating disc or thin pole.
One monumental ravine and eight smaller cuts break the pillar around all 360 degrees, while the public railway reads as a shelf, cave and shaft excavated into the rock.
Two continuous summit railway bands encircle the town and remain visually separate from the live tile route.

featureReviews.notes: The island is recognizably a floating red-rock mesa, but its cliff underside remains a regular cylinder and the far buttes are still simplified terraces rather than fractured canyon formations.
The central tower now leads the composition, but reads as one dark block with a thin spire instead of the source's layered station wings, porches, windows, trim, flag, and warm timber articulation.
Both railway rails and sleepers are real geometry and the train animates, but the locomotive is too small and the railway lacks ballast, tunnel framing, switchwork and foreground prominence.
Water tower and windmill silhouettes are visible and the five landmark families exist, but sheriff, signal yard and Rail Nest architecture need much more meso detail and stronger framing.

Fences, pebbles and cactus variation were added, yet most surfaces remain broad flat colour fields; missing fractured edge rocks, scrub clumps, crates, signs, timber trim, rail ballast and atmospheric distance layers dominate the mismatch.

The double rails, sleepers, two-sided moving train and tangent-aligned open tunnel are real geometry. The train remains visually small and simple against the source, and tunnel portal readability needs a dedicated survey.

All five families remain distinct from four angles, with water tower and windmill strongest. Sheriff, signal yard and smaller depot structures still need richer roof, signage, porch and ground-story articulation.

Cacti, fences, pebbles, crates, fractured edges and warm sky are present, but the scene is still broad low-detail procedural colour compared with the source's dense rock, timber, rail ballast, vegetation and atmospheric layering.

Left and right surveys prove real depth, side windows and two-sided train construction. The rear survey exposes an under-authored Union Station service wall, so the new 360-degree gate is not yet passed.

featureReviews.notes: The user-approved tall mountain support now keeps nearly full width to its base, and attached shoulder masses replace much of the two-drum silhouette. The broad horizontal cylinder bands remain visible and still need a later material/form breakup pass.

One dominant full-height ravine, eight secondary cuts and eight short tributaries are visible across the four surveys. The monumental cut reads clearly; some minor cuts still rely on dark overlays rather than true recessed cliff topology.

The railway remains a shelf-and-gallery public transport line with bridge supports across the major chasm. The close canyon camera proves continuity, but the rails are visually thin and the shaft interiors need stronger rock engineering detail.

Frontier town, railway, red rock and sunset identity remain recognizable, but literal source composition diverges because the user explicitly replaced the source's broad floating plateau with a tall pillar and spiral mission. The sculpt spec must record this accepted exception rather than treating it as an implementation defect.
Warm red-rock value separation improved around canyon lips and shoulders, but the pillar is still very dark and horizontally repetitive compared with the source's luminous, varied sandstone.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The deterministic Tier-1 and multi-angle volume checks pass, proving stable framing and real 3D volume only. Agent vision finds a meaningful structural delta from pass 54: the broad tangential sheets are gone, rounded sunlit stones interrupt the cuboids, and the right/rear silhouettes are less cylindrical. The result still falls short of the approved goal because erosion columns are too regular, rail-adjacent benches are sparse, and landmark structures remain low-detail. Refine-code is therefore retained.

featureReviews.notes: The full-width pillar, one monumental ravine and the three-turn public railway now read as one structure. Four-part gallery shells add recessed back walls, under-shelf rock and flanking buttresses, so the route is visibly excavated rather than suspended. Rock cadence is still more regular than the approved goal and belongs in form refinement.

Union Station remains dominant while the windmill, water tower, signal yard and sheriff archive keep distinct structural silhouettes in the overview and four surveys. Their timber trim, rear service detail and lived-in ground dressing remain below final quality.

The engine, tender and two coaches are independently posed on the rail centreline and remain legible in the rear descent survey. The train is correctly small at full-column scale; close-up wheel, rod and steam richness is deferred.

Near and far butte bands remain fixed in world space and recede through the warm background. Their silhouettes are structurally layered but visibly simple, so form refinement must replace the repeated chimney cadence with broader Monument Valley groups.

The terrain edits are presentation-only and retain the unchanged canonical 36-tile transforms, reward objects and token clearance. Full-column inspection intentionally hides board actors, while the gameplay overview preserves them.

Engine, tender and two coaches remain independently sampled on the route with natural spacing and tangent changes. The train reads correctly in overview and orbit views; close material and steam refinement remains later work.

Far scenery now uses broad tiered mesa bases, crowns, attached spires and overlapping continental shelves positioned on the descending camera horizon. It no longer reads as a row of detached floating chimneys, though the silhouettes remain simpler than the source.
All form changes remain presentation-only around the unchanged canonical route. Board tiles, token clearance, rail centreline and landmark placements remain intact.
